title: M1, M2: approval prompts and AskUserQuestion never surface in Home. The row reads 'running' for 120 s, then the session is dropped while its dialog is still open.
repro: Launch vibepet on the isolated fleet root and click Net: Home opens.
Put kestrel into a fresh permission prompt, or beacon into a fresh AskUserQuestion (Esc the old dialog, then fleet rearm).
Poll Home's rows every 250 ms for 3 min and compare with `fleet status --json` (registry waiting / waitingFor).
expected: Within 3 s the row reads needs-you. For an approval it shows the command and Approve; for a question, the question text, the options and Reply. It is ordered by wait and stays until answered. Sessions already blocked when the pet launches appear with their true wait.
actual: 0 of 4 fresh dialogs were ever shown as needing the user (kestrel ×2, beacon ×2). While each dialog was up, the transcript held no pending tool_use. The row read 'running' (green dot, no ask, no action) for 119–121 s and was then removed while the dialog stayed open. The registry turned waiting (permission prompt / input needed) 1.3–1.7 s after each prompt. As found, kestrel and beacon had been blocked 79 min: Home said 'No live sessions. Start Claude Code anywhere and I'll pick it up.' and the pet was calm with a grey LED. Typing /jump kestrel answered 'No session matches'.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F4 approval + AskUserQuestion rows (never, n=2 each)
truth: kestrel registry waiting(permission prompt) since 00:32:53Z, 01:54:40.790Z and 02:03:49.383Z. beacon waiting(input needed) since 00:32:56Z, 01:54:41.359Z and 02:13:42.729Z. The last transcript record was the user prompt every time; no tool process.

title: M7: a finished session disappears from Home 5 min after its turn while it is still alive at its prompt, and /jump cannot find it
repro: Let a member finish a turn (vibepet or atlas) while Home is open.
Wait 5 min.
Type '/jump vibepet' in the composer.
expected: Finished sessions stay listed (for example as done/idle, oldest first) until the user acts or the session exits. /jump finds them.
actual: vibepet was removed 301.7 s after its end_turn, atlas 302.6 s after. Both stayed registry idle (alive at the prompt). As found, vibepet (done 51 min) had no row. '/jump vibepet' answered 'No session matches “vibepet”.' Only ⋯ → Theater… still lists these sessions, as replays.
truth: vibepet end_turn 01:55:03.362Z, registry idle. atlas end_turn 02:02:56.993Z, registry idle. Both claude processes running.

title: M13, CH36: the Now list overflows at 4 rows. The 4th row is cut and Record/Today/localhost scroll out of view while ~250 px of empty chat area sits below. Rows are capped at 8.
repro: With 4 listed sessions (vibepet, ember, atlas, delta), click Net.
Look at the Now list without scrolling.
Scroll the list to find the footer.
expected: With 5–15 sessions, every live session (up to 15) and the localhost/recording footer are visible without scrolling, or the panel grows into its free height.
actual: 3 of 4 rows are fully visible; delta's row is cut in half. Record a short, Today and both localhost servers are below the fold (#now max-height 46% of the panel), while the chat area under it is empty. The list renders at most 8 rows (renderHome slice(0, 8)), so at 9+ sessions the rest are never shown.
truth: 01:58:43Z: vibepet done, ember loop, atlas working, delta fan-out listed. kestrel and beacon blocked but not listed.

title: M8: a /loop session between fires reads 'done Nm ago' with the your-move yellow dot
repro: Start ember's '/loop 5m run ./tick.sh' (fleet rearm ember).
Open Home between fires.
expected: A looping/scheduled state that is not 'done' and not your move, with the time since the last fire (and the next fire, when known).
actual: 'ember · done 4m ago' (01:52Z) and 'ember · done 10m ago' (01:58:43Z), both with a yellow dot. Nothing says it is a loop.
truth: registry idle with exactly one live cron job (fleet loop check OK). Fires at 01:48:21Z, 01:53:07Z and 01:57:52Z.

title: M9: an exited session reads 'running' for 2 min after its claude process is gone, then silently disappears
repro: With Home open, exit a member (fleet pause ember → /exit).
Watch its row for 3 min.
expected: Within 3 s the row says the session ended or exited, or it is removed with a note. It never says 'running'.
actual: From 1.9 s after the exit, the row read 'running · ember · 0s … 1m 58s' (green) until 122 s, then vanished with no note.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F2 exited→stops reading running (122450 ms)
docs/ultra/round-1/raw/S1/tt2.json (ember running at 02:00:52Z; truth: claude not running)
truth: claude process gone and registry removed at 01:59:35.9Z (fleet status: claude not running).

title: M11: clicking a row (go to its terminal) fails for a tmux session with no feedback in the panel, and puts a 'claude --resume' command on the clipboard
repro: Open Home with a tmux-hosted session listed (atlas).
Click the row body.
expected: Its tmux pane comes forward. Failing that, the panel states the failure in the row and offers something that works. The clipboard never gets a command that would start a second claude on a live session.
actual: jump returned {ok:false, cmd:'cd …/atlas && claude --resume <id>'} in 171 ms, and the clipboard write was intercepted. The only feedback was the bubble 'atlas: couldn't find its terminal — resume command copied', drawn behind the panel. The row shows nothing.
evidence: docs/ultra/round-1/packs/S1/timings.json F3 row click (249 ms, ok:false)
truth: atlas alive in tmux pane vp-atlas, registry idle.

title: T1: turns shorter than the 3 s refresh are never shown. 2 of 3 /loop fires were invisible, with no done signal.
repro: Keep Home open while ember's loop fires (2.2 s turns).
Watch ember's row and Net's bubble.
expected: Each turn shows (running → done), or at least the done age resets and the finish is announced.
actual: The fires at 01:53:06.8–01:53:09.0Z and 01:57:52.3–01:57:54.6Z were never shown. The row kept 'done 5m ago' / 'done 9m ago', with no bubble or sound.

title: M3: row ages count from when this pet first saw the phase, not from the session's own timestamps. A loop idle 49 s reads 'done 10m ago'; a 42 s question reads 'waiting 1m'.
repro: Open Home after ember's loop has fired unseen (see r1-S1-07), and when kestrel ends a turn with a question.
Compare each row's age with the registry statusUpdatedAt and the record timestamps.
expected: Ages from the session's registry and record timestamps, with seconds under a minute.
actual: ember read 'done 10m ago' at 01:58:43Z, 49 s after its last turn ended. kestrel read 'waiting 1m' 1.45 s after its question and still at 42 s (minimum 1m, rounded).

title: M4: a long tool's clock freezes at '0s' after 90 s. The atlas build read '0s' from 93 s to its end at 9 min.
repro: Rearm atlas (9-min foreground build) and open Home.
Read its row after 90 s.
expected: 'running · 4m 50s', the time since the tool started.
actual: 'atlas · 0s' from 92.96 s after the tool started until the turn ended at 541 s.
truth: registry busy since 01:53:53.784Z, Bash ./build.sh pending, 3 tool processes.

title: T2: with Home open, Net's speech bubble is drawn behind the panel
repro: Open Home.
Wait for a bubble (atlas finishing, or a failed row jump).
expected: The bubble is visible above the panel, or its message appears in the panel.
actual: At 02:02:59Z 'atlas is done' rendered under the composer (the element at the bubble's centre was #chatInput). The jump-failure bubble was hidden the same way.

title: Home rows show no fan-out gauge or subagent count: delta with 3 running subagents reads 'delta · 33s', like a single session
repro: Rearm delta (3 parallel subagents).
Open Home.
expected: The row shows a gauge or count (3 open, n done, oldest running age), as the hover roster does.
actual: No gauge, count or subagent names, although the app's own snapshot has fanout {total 3, open 3, done 0}.
truth: registry busy since 01:58:09.7Z, 3 subagents each running ./slow.sh, 9 tool processes.

title: Home orders rows within a rank newest first, so the longest wait sinks, while the jump key orders oldest first
repro: Have two sessions in the same rank (two done rows).
Open Home and read the order.
expected: The oldest wait first within each of needs, stuck and done, in the same order as the jump key and roster.
actual: At 02:02:59Z 'atlas · done just now' was listed above 'delta · done 2m ago'; at 02:03:53Z atlas (1m) was above delta (3m). byUrgency sorts newest first (b.since − a.since); pending() sorts oldest first.

title: A single click opens Home in 236 ms (a fixed 220 ms double-click wait), over the 150 ms panel budget
repro: Click Net once, then Esc. Repeat ×5.
Measure mouseup → panel shown and → first painted frame (renderer clock).
expected: Open in ≤ 150 ms.
actual: Median 221.4 ms to shown and 236 ms to first paint (n=5, load 2.9–3.2). A double click opens in 21 ms. Closing by clicking Net also waits 233 ms.

title: Keyboard focus on a row button is wiped by the 3 s re-render, and rows are not focusable, so rows cannot be used from the keyboard
repro: Open Home.
Shift+Tab from the composer to a row's ◎ button.
Wait 3 s.
expected: Focus stays put, and every row is reachable and actionable by keyboard (Tab, arrows or number keys).
actual: Focus fell back to the page body 2.5 s later, when the tick rebuilt #now. Row bodies have no focus stop.
truth: delta done, idle at its prompt.

title: Tab off the end of the panel, or Shift+Tab off its start, closes Home
repro: Open Home (focus is in the composer).
Press Tab once, or Shift+Tab until past the ⋯ button.
expected: Focus wraps inside the panel.
actual: Focus leaves the page (activeElement = body), the window blurs and Home closes. Seen with trusted key events in the test instance.

title: CH37: no needs-me filter and no unread state in Home. Blocked, done and running sessions share one scrolling list.
repro: Open Home with several sessions listed.
expected: A Needs me / All filter or grouping (needs, working, idle/done) and unread state that persists until seen.
actual: One flat list sorted by rank with no filter, grouping headers or unread markers. Done rows look like needs-you rows (r1-S1-17), and hidden sessions are uncounted (r1-S1-02).

title: Done rows and needs-you rows share the same yellow dot, and the header dot is always green
repro: Open Home with one needs-you row and two done rows.
expected: Distinct colour or shape for 'needs you' vs 'finished', and a header indicator that reflects the fleet.
actual: kestrel (needs) and atlas/delta (done) all have yellow dots. The header dot stays green while sessions are blocked or hidden.
truth: kestrel waiting on a question; atlas and delta finished.

title: The row's state label is its smallest, dimmest text (11 px grey), while the session name repeats in bold ('ember' / 'ember · done …')
repro: Open Home with an untitled session (ember) listed.
expected: The state and wait read first, at a glance. The name is not duplicated.
actual: The state label is 11 px #858c9c on #16181c (5.27:1). The title is bold 13 px and repeats the name when there is no title.

title: The header names one repo ('no repo', 'ember/main', 'atlas/main') that changes with whichever session was last active
repro: Open Home at different moments while several sessions run.
expected: A header that summarises the fleet (for example '2 need you · 3 running'), or no repo at all.
actual: It read 'no repo · claude code' while 3 sessions were live, then 'ember/main', then 'atlas/main'.

title: Row actions are bare glyphs (▶ ✓ ◎) whose meaning is only in hover titles. ✓ (mark goal done) sits where an approve button would be expected.
repro: Open Home and look at a row's buttons.
expected: Labelled or self-evident actions; ✓ not confusable with approve.
actual: ▶ = replay, ✓ = mark goal done, ◎ = set goal, each explained only by a tooltip.

title: CH21: Home closes whenever the pet window loses focus, so each trip to a terminal (needed because blocks cannot be resolved from the pet) costs a reopen
repro: Open Home.
Click into another app (here emulated with a window blur event: the test instance never holds the OS focus).
Click Net again.
expected: Home stays open, or can be pinned, while the user checks a terminal.
actual: Home closes on blur. Reopening takes another click and 236 ms. Text typed in the composer survives.
